title: Pecan Bourbon Whole Trout Board
seoTitle: Pecan Bourbon Whole Trout Board | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Trout on the grill—not salmon, not plank—maple bourbon char for the hall
subtitle: Whole butterflied trout, maple-bourbon glaze, and char for ten
description: Whole butterflied rainbow trout brush with maple-bourbon glaze, grill in baskets until skin crisps and flesh reads 145°F, and finish with dill and lemon.

steps.title: Build maple-bourbon glaze
steps.instruction: Simmer maple syrup, bourbon, mustard, soy, and garlic until slightly thickened. Cool before brushing. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use fresh thyme, pecans, shallots, fresh sage as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Prep trout
steps.instruction: Pat trout completely dry inside and out. Season with salt and pepper. Brush flesh lightly with half the glaze. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium, 375°F. Oil fish basket well. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill trout
steps.instruction: Grill trout in basket flesh-side down 6–8 minutes until skin crisps. Flip carefully. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for fish, 145°F for shrimp until opaque on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Brush glaze on flesh side and grill 4–6 minutes until 145°F at thickest part and flesh flakes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest before plating
steps.instruction: Rest trout 3 minutes off heat. Transfer to platters flesh-side up. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 140°F
steps.instruction: Hold covered at 140°F up to 12 minutes max. Fish dries fast above 145°F hold. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Serve with dill
steps.instruction: Scatter dill and serve with lemon wedges. One whole trout per firefighter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Fish basket prevents trout from breaking on grates.
Simmer bourbon glaze to cook off alcohol before brushing.
145°F hold max—trout tightens into rubber above that.
tonightSpread: Maple bourbon grilled trout with dill and lemon.
leftovers: Flake trout into trout salad sandwiches.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Trout cooks faster than salmon and feels distinct on the menu. Whole fish on the grill impresses the crew and holds briefly at 140°F between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Pat trout dry. Grill medium 375°F in fish baskets 6–8 minutes per side. Hold covered at 140°F up to 12 minutes max. Glaze in last 2 minutes only.
